paras: Diploglossus garridoi, also known commonly as the Cuban small-eared galliwasp, is a species of lizard in the family Diploglossidae. The species is endemic to Cuba.
The specific name, garridoi, is in honor of Cuban herpetologist Orlando H. Garrido.
D. garridoi is found in Granma Province, Cuba.
The preferred natural habitat of D. garridoi is forest, at altitudes of 600–1,700 m (2,000–5,600 ft).
